title: Low status of the musician in show business
summary: Musicians are not invited to cast parties.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: The idea of a college, such as you suggested, would be
fine, but it depends on a lot. It depends on the situation, how much they wanted me; that has a lot to do with it. If I had to go and prove myself, no thanks. I don't want to do that.

As a matter of fact, I don't even get insulted at things like that, because most people don't know that I exist or have existed, they simply don't know, the people I encounter and that doesn't bother me at all. There's always a lack of respect that goes along with these things. There should be the respect that is accorded anybody just because they're a human being, but I've been much too involved with show business and the lowest form of life on their scale is the musician; and I wonder why. Partly because they don't
like to pay anybody, and secondly I think the jokes of those so-called comedians through the years have not helped things. I think that has done a lot for that.

This past show is just one of many, they have cast parties and they never invite the musicians--never. The only one that did was the one in Washington; that's the only one where I ever recall that they did that.
The show business scene, as far as actors and chorus lines and what have you, that's a whole other world.
It's another world and it's all sick. It's no good; and TV isn't any better.
The only thing about TV, when it comes to me, you don't deal with anybody except the producer, but the purpose is the same.
It's a piece of musical wallpaper.
But then records are the same thing, record companies do just that.
